match.reason: The bank point covers only justifying a conclusion with evidence and its gaps, while the new point also needs ethical values such as fairness and weighing environmental, economic and social effects of actions, and it is pitched at Year 10 rather than Years 7 and 8.

draft.title: Drawing conclusions and choosing actions
card: A conclusion is a statement that answers your inquiry question. A sound conclusion rests on the evidence you collected, not on a guess or a hunch.
A geographer also thinks about ethical values, such as fairness. A conclusion should consider whether people or places are treated fairly.
After a conclusion, a geographer may suggest an action, which is something to be done about the issue.
A good action weighs its environmental, economic and social effects. These are the effects on nature, on money and jobs, and on people and communities.
draft.remember: A sound conclusion rests on evidence and considers fairness. A good action weighs environmental, economic and social effects.

a.q: Which conclusion is best supported by evidence?
opts: Our survey of 40 shoppers shows most walk to the market
I think most people in town probably walk to the market
Everyone knows that walking to the market is better
The market should be closed because I dislike the crowds
a.why: The first conclusion is based on survey results that were collected. The second is tempting because it sounds careful, but it is only a guess with no evidence behind it.
a.clue: Which one points to something that was collected?

b.q: A council plans to build a new skate park beside a creek in Wodonga. Which question shows a geographer weighing the economic effect of this action?
opts: How much will the skate park cost to build and run?
Will the creek and its wildlife be disturbed?
Will young people from all suburbs be able to reach it?
Will families feel safe and welcome there?
b.why: Cost to build and run is about money, so it is an economic effect. The question about the creek is tempting, but it is about the environment. The other two are about people and fairness, which are social.
b.clue: Economic effects are about money and jobs.

a.best: Our survey of 40 shoppers shows most walk to the market

b.best: How much will the skate park cost to build and run?

problems.detail: The why calls the options 'the first conclusion' and 'the second', but options are shown in random order. A student may see a different option in those positions. Name the options by their content instead, such as 'the survey of 40 shoppers' and 'I think most people probably walk'.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate and at the right level. The only problem is that Why (a) refers to options by position ('first', 'second'), which will not match the random order students see.
